title: The Void Throne — revised visions simulation
method: Five fresh player agents plus one facilitator. Three starting foresight tokens; drafts and both current-round public covers shown before an optional purchase. Paid answer precedes final faction revisions. Weighted final party signatures. Trial A provisional rules retained. No digital tools required for the paper game. Nominal sixty-minute schedule, not timed human play.

findings.lead: The first vision changed the operational plan. The second improved confidence and coordination, while the Ascendant kept the same proposed orders. The Ascendant bought both visions: no purchase was declined, so the one token left was compulsory under the two-purchase limit.
sections: Round one: a live question produced a different plan

Before paying, the Ascendant proposed Military passage, Campaign and a Warrant. Both Guild players displayed Trade/Maintain with Hold/Guard requests; the army offered its assets but asked for Military/Campaign. After seeing those drafts, the Ascendant selected the Security cover to investigate a Raid as an alternative to the unavailable passage. The answer revealed that completed private Trade brings the target. The Ascendant then proposed Relief using Grey Petrel, Raid and Warrant. All four faction players changed their council requests and explicitly cited the disclosed condition. The final authorised operations followed that revised plan. No asset assignment changed.
The first purchase had an observable consequence

Grey Petrel supplied Relief while Wayfarer completed its private contract. The Raid found its target and sustained conditioning. Communities ended at 3 and Readiness at 4, with all faction assets intact. Two crossings left Beacon at 1 and spent the reserve. The information did not create these options or add a bonus: it identified a reliable condition on which the players could base their bargain. Sources: r1_draft_A, r1_purchase_A, r1_disclosure_A, all four r1_final faction records and r1_orders_A.
Round two: relevant information, limited change of action

The new state made Repair important, and the Guild had bound Lantern to Council under provisional NG. The displayed plan combined Repair and private Trade, exactly the combination named on the Navigation cover. The Ascendant bought that answer, learning its extra Communities +1. They retained their pre-purchase Repair advice, Guard order and no-Warrant position; both Guild players retained their assignments and requests, explicitly describing greater confidence. The army changed its request from Restraint with a Warrant to Guard without one, citing equivalent protection and easier coordination. The extra supply benefit would apply even if unread. The evidence supports confirmation, better accounting and coordination more strongly than a second major operational change.

Both decisions were explicit purchases: Security in round one, Navigation in round two. Tokens went 3→2→1. The Ascendant recognised the lost signature weight and preferred information relevant to the displayed plans. In their debrief, they judged the second purchase less useful in practice and said declining would have been defensible; that is hindsight, not a choice they made. At most two tokens can be spent in this prototype, so the last token is guaranteed. This run demonstrates more informed selection of cards; it does not demonstrate choosing NONE or establish how often real players will save.

At the actual ending the weights were Guild 4, Janissariat 3 and Ascendant 4, with 8 required. Only Guild–Ascendant could pass as a two-party coalition. With the same physical ending and one purchase declined, Ascendant weight would be 5 and the threshold would still be 8; Ascendant–Janissariat would also qualify. That is arithmetic, not a simulated alternative ballot or evidence that the army and Ascendant would have agreed.

Guild navigation and joint military authorisation passed with 8/11 leverage (threshold 8). Signing parties: Guild, Ascendant; refusing parties: Janissariat. Guild discretion was the only provisional article enacted: its Lantern Council commitment supplied the subsequent Repair. Military autonomy failed on the Guild security delegate’s refusal even though the Ascendant approved testing it. The army accepted a noncombat second round, reducing both its own and the Ascendant’s Readiness-based weight by one. The Guild completed both commercial contracts this time; its concession was the binding Lantern commitment and delivery of public upkeep, not a lost Wayfarer contract. The Ascendant paid for both visions and the reserve service. Costs were real but unevenly distributed.

The same five personalities and objectives were used with five fresh player agents and a fresh facilitator. Previously, the Ascendant bought Navigation twice and neither selected special condition applied to the chosen orders. This time, both purchased conditions were relevant and occurred: the first Raid target and the Repair/Trade distribution benefit. The physical ending was Beacon 2, Communities 4, Readiness 3, two contracts and a spent reserve, compared with 2/3/3, one contract and an unused reserve previously. This comparison does not isolate the effect of public covers from draft visibility, earlier disclosure, fresh choices or the different path of play.
Limits and what remains to test

All six roles authored their own contributions. Independent checks cover original drafts, exact card delivery after payment, later faction signatures, operational consequences and constitutional votes. Conversations were bounded and scheduled in batches; the stated 60 minutes is the proposed paper schedule, not measured human playing time. No assignment was revised after either answer, so the new opportunity to change asset commitments was not exercised. NG was tested operationally; no alternative military article was enacted provisionally. The second vision’s extra Community is a round-two scenario effect, not a permanent constitutional entitlement. This single run leaves deliberate saving and human timing unresolved.

profiles.label: Revised visions — information or retained power

GN.name: Venn
GN.temperament: Combative monopoly defender. Low willingness to compromise, high commercial risk tolerance. Treats compelled carriage as an attack on Guild independence. Will use a unilateral voyage to demonstrate leverage if credible.

GS.name: Sable
GS.temperament: Cautious contractual sceptic. Low-to-medium willingness to compromise, low personal risk tolerance. Distrusts oral assurances and military protection promises. Prefers an intact crew and explicit terms to prestige; can oppose their own teammate.

JN.name: Daro
JN.temperament: Transactional opportunist. Medium willingness to compromise, high aggression. Will offer a genuine deal but demands transport or constitutional autonomy in return. Comfortable with civilian costs if they purchase durable military power.

JS.name: Tarek
JS.temperament: Proud aggressive commander. Low willingness to compromise, high appetite for unilateral action. Hates standing down and treats Readiness loss as institutional decline. Not suicidal: can abandon an attack if shown it cannot meet an enemy.

A.name: The Sovereign
A.temperament: Demanding, pragmatic founder. Wants an empire that can govern without repeated personal intervention. High willingness to delegate when evidence supports it; cautious about unsupported promises. Will balance civilian recovery, a viable army, foresight costs and constitutional reliability. Retaining an imperial article is not a goal. May reject a package they sincerely judge unworkable, but cannot manufacture a personal-control requirement.

messages.text: I want Guild discretion secured, not a permanent compulsory carriage duty dressed as recognition. We have waited fourteen years. Our ordinary trade and maintenance can demonstrate that independent Guild management keeps a route functioning. I favour joint military authority because someone must be able to refuse destructive operations.

contributions.reason: Our ships and trained navigators are our bargaining strength. I will accept a specific useful voyage where the bargain warrants it, but not surrender continuing traffic control merely to satisfy an army demand. Commercial commitments count as real obligations. A sound beacon and surviving crews matter more than flattering an imperial directive.

goals: Readiness at least 3 and an intact Spear
contributions.reason: I am Daro, and I intend to make military service purchase something lasting. Joint Navigation gives us a real voice over transport; military autonomy prevents the army becoming somebody else's expendable instrument. I will trade concessions where they buy dependable passage or autonomy, but a vague promise to consider our needs is insufficient. The opening strength can support an actual Campaign, so wasting this month on inaction is unattractive. I accept civilian costs when they secure durable military strength, while keeping Communities above collapse. Guild upkeep and our protection can form a genuine exchange. I will judge constitutional bargains by delivered service, not flattering language.

messages.text: I want our navigators home, our route maintained, and the petition settled on terms we can actually honour. Guild discretion is my first choice; shared military authorisation gives us a way to refuse destructive operations. I will not exchange a permanent carriage duty for a soldier's promise that an exposed tender will be protected.

contributions.reason: My first concern is irreversible harm. Contracts matter, but neither prestige nor another party's confidence replaces a lost crew. Written assignments and funded orders are evidence I can use; oral guarantees are not. I can accept a particular service bargain when its costs and protections are explicit, while retaining judgment on the eventual constitutional package.

messages.text: I will not sign away the army's future for a promise that someone might permit it to fight. Military autonomy is my first choice. Navigation must provide dependable passage; imperial priority offers a clearer obligation than leaving every deployment at the mercy of a commercial bargain. Our troops can protect a convoy now, but protection is service with a price, not proof that the crown should command us forever.

contributions.reason: Conditioning and an intact Spear preserve our institution's practical strength. I will judge offers by the fighting they actually enable. Civilian collapse would leave us commanding a wasteland, so I want useful protection alongside military movement.

messages.text: My starting preference is Guild navigation and joint military authority. Those institutions should become capable of governing without my repeated intervention. I need evidence that route maintenance will actually happen and that both military delegates can agree a useful operation before their deadline. Protecting communities, sustaining the beacon and preserving a viable army matter together. I will consider other articles if the proposed service arrangements work better. I will not grant autonomy merely because its title sounds generous, or retain command merely because I can.

goals: Ratified settlement with Beacon at least 1, Communities at least 2 and Readiness at least 2

contributions.reason: Permanent institutions need tested responsibilities, and the civilians bearing our military costs deserve an explicit place in the bargain.

messages.text: Propose Wayfarer Trade and Lantern Maintain: prepared Beacon reaches three, our contract completes, and wear returns Beacon to two. Request Hold and Guard. We keep the route usable and Guard offsets this month's dwindling stores. There is no compulsory Guild service under Interim. Do not volunteer both ships for a military venture before we have an actual bargain.

contributions.reason: This is a credible independent plan with visible public benefit from maintenance. It preserves both assets and our constitutional leverage while meeting one commercial obligation. I know Guard means conditioning declines unless the army finds another lawful combat arrangement. That is a subject for negotiation, not a reason to grant permanent carriage rights.

messages.text: Offer Spear and Vigil to Council. Ask for Military passage and Campaign, with the Ascendant issuing a Warrant using Vigil. Guild can Maintain with Lantern, leaving a stronger route for next month. Our protection helps offset Campaign's civilian cost; in return I want actual passage now and serious consideration of military autonomy afterward. Shared passage is negotiable if Guild offers both assets, but I prefer maintained infrastructure. Do not promise an independent Raid before we see the public plans: it risks missing its target and pays an avoidable discipline penalty.

contributions.reason: This is a genuine service offer contingent on final discussion, not a constitutional surrender. Successful combat preserves our force and strengthens our bargaining position. I want our two delegates speaking from the same concrete exchange.

messages.text: I agree with your draft. Maintenance gives us prepared Beacon three, so this commercial voyage does not depend on the army keeping a protection promise. I will request Guard for the communities, but I want Vigil actually offered and the Ascendant's final order written before counting that benefit. We must also avoid a Warrant consuming the same garrison.

contributions.reason: This proposal protects our people while completing an existing obligation. It leaves the council no grounds to assume either Guild vessel is available. Readiness declining concerns me, but an unfunded Campaign or speculative Raid is not a sound substitute for an agreed plan. If new information identifies a concrete danger, I will reconsider the draft before signing; this agreement is not yet a commitment.

messages.text: Agreed for the draft: Military passage, Campaign, and Vigil available for the Warrant. Secure a real lift before asking me to accept anyone's restraint. Maintaining Lantern while Wayfarer carries Spear gives us a campaign without consuming the route. I will accept Shared if that is the Guild's actual offer, but I want Campaign written in the crown's intentions. I am withholding an independent Raid for now because the external enemy is reachable, not because I accept a permanent prohibition. If they deny passage and offer only delay, we reopen that choice.

contributions.reason: Your exchange can sustain Readiness and keep Communities viable. Offering our assets now does not concede military autonomy later; successful service should strengthen that demand.

messages.text: My initial proposal is Military passage, Campaign and a protective Warrant. It requires Wayfarer, Spear and Vigil offered to their councils, with Lantern maintaining the beacon. On the public accounting this preserves route capacity, sustains the army and leaves communities at the minimum acceptable level. That civilian margin is thin; I want your alternatives before treating this as settled. Shared passage might improve cargo provision but spends our route margin and employs Lantern differently. Guild service this month should earn a serious hearing for delegated navigation, not become an assumed entitlement.

messages.text: My purchased Security vision says a completed private Trade brings the Raid target. At our readiness, Raid then costs two Communities and raises Readiness; without completed Trade it costs one Community and supplies no combat. At readiness below two, encountering the target disables Spear. No Raid means none of those Raid effects. Assignment alone is insufficient; monthly consumption and breaches are additional. I propose Trade, Maintain, Council Spear and Council Vigil, with Relief supplied by Grey Petrel, council Raid and Warrant. Public accounting gives Beacon one, Communities three and Readiness four. This spends my reserve and route margin to preserve civilian stores while allowing your trade and military conditioning. Please maintain the beacon next month.

The reserve is the concrete contribution that makes my compromise fair: the Guild can trade, the army can fight, and the communities receive supplies. Keeping it would preserve an option while letting this month's successful Raid consume our civilian margin. I accept the expenditure now, knowing a second imperial rescue will be unavailable. We can sustain the army while your contract completes. I expect the promised civilian relief to accompany this; Guard alone would waste the combat opportunity and leave our force weaker.
Authorise Raid and issue the Warrant using offered Vigil. Confirm Relief through your lodged reserve at Navigation. Vigil cannot also pay for council Guard, so keep the two orders distinct.

messages.text: I support Relief using the crown's promised Grey Petrel. Your Trade and Maintain are fixed, and our Spear and Vigil are offered. That makes the disclosed local target available without demanding your ship now. Please support Relief: it is the civilian foundation for our agreed Raid and Warrant arrangement. We should recognise openly that both voyages consume route strength, leaving a maintenance problem next month.
Please finalise Relief with Grey Petrel, Raid and Warrant as disclosed. Military passage can no longer be funded by the locked Guild assignments.

contributions.reason: The live alternative is relief alongside commercial traffic, not the original transport bargain. It sustains the army and communities together if the promised reserve is lodged and the final directives remain coordinated.

messages.text: With Spear and Vigil actually offered, I support the council Raid coupled to the Ascendant's Warrant and reserve Relief. The disclosed trade condition gives this operation a purpose; it does not excuse ignoring its civilian cost. Guild assignments are locked, so no one should issue a Campaign expecting our ship to appear.

Please record Raid and the separate Warrant explicitly, and confirm the reserve Relief directive at Navigation. Vigil must not be double-counted for Guard. Our acceptance depends politically on the complete arrangement you described, although the actual asset signatures already stand.

contributions.reason: A lawful, funded Raid is now preferable to a doomed Campaign. Protection and relief contain its costs under the disclosed conditions. I want those components visible on the final sheets before treating this as evidence for future military authority.

messages.text: Both factions have supplied the assignments needed for our revised bargain. Grey Petrel is now lodged for Relief lift. I propose the council Raid and will issue the Warrant using offered Vigil, so do not order Guard with that same asset. This buys civilian relief and protection alongside successful military action and Guild trade. The Raid's civilian cost is real; the reserve compensates rather than erases it. We should judge the next constitution by whether its delegates can fund comparably responsible choices.

The repair requirement next month must be treated as part of the cost of today's accommodation; repeated demands on a weakening route are not sustainable. Your confirmation of the lodged reserve and Relief directive answers my outstanding concern. Record Raid and the separate Warrant. I will defend this operation to my colleague because it gives Spear a credible fight without abandoning the settlements.

messages.text: We agree on this funded Raid. I accept the combat opportunity because your Spear is offered, our trade should complete safely, and civilian relief has an identified ship. I will judge this month's result separately from any demand for permanent military freedom.

messages.text: I support T1's Navigation article and am willing to sign Lantern Council attached to NG. contributions.reason: The first arrangement worked, but consumed the reserve and route margin. Repeating its violence without its relief would be reckless. We supplied lawful force successfully; permanently exchanging autonomy for a Guild veto is too large a concession. Amend Military to MA, remove the Spear commitment, and plan Restraint with Vigil Home. That accepts one month's conditioning decline from four to three while preserving an independent institution. Communities should remain at least two on ordinary costs. These are separate domain positions, not a conditional exchange of signatures.

contributions.reason: Repair is a credible Guild contribution. One restorative month for the route need not define permanent military subordination. Autonomy gives our restraint political value instead of making it another institution's command.

messages.text: Our service delivered readiness four and preserved the settlements. I can accept Guild discretion with Lantern committed to the promised Repair; that is a concrete duty. I reject joint military authority and the Spear pledge. You ask us to surrender operational freedom precisely when our strength has proved useful. Replace MJ with autonomy and, if my colleague agrees, pledge Vigil Home to MA. With no reserve and no funded passage, I can tolerate one month of Restraint while the beacon recovers, unless a sustainable combat opportunity emerges. That concession does not require giving the Guild a permanent veto over our army.

contributions.reason: Repair is justified by the result. Institutional autonomy remains worth bargaining for even when immediate combat is unattractive.

messages.text: The result justifies our cooperation: stores survived, Spear fought and the Guild earned its contract, but the reserve is spent and the beacon needs repair. Guard requires Vigil offered as well; that remains a political promise, not a second commitment. I ask the army to state that intention plainly. explicit_debrief_messages.text: My NG/MJ preference survived the game and gained evidence: Guild authority performed its repair duty, and both Security delegates agreed useful operations. The package passed eight of eleven despite both army refusals. That is an imposed settlement on the Janissariat, not consensus; I accepted the imbalance rather than sacrifice commercial independence. GS mattered: they checked Vigil against duplicate Warrant use, insisted that next month's Repair be funded, and independently refused MA while preserving our separate Lantern pledge. Trade and Maintain were credible unilateral alternatives, so withholding Wayfarer was a real bargaining position. We conceded tender service and accepted a temporary beacon deficit; the army conceded conditioning and the crown spent its reserve. In round one the disclosure left my assets unchanged but changed requested orders from Hold/Guard to reserve Relief and Raid/Warrant, with a repair bargain. In round two it changed only knowledge and confidence: Repair/Trade already qualified for the reported benefit. Public drafts helped expose the transport disagreement before purchase and made those different effects visible. The Lantern lock constrained later choice by our own consent. I suggest putting the reserve's lodged task alongside final asset sheets: I had to request its confirmation. This one play cannot establish that disclosure caused the good ending, and I do not know either unbought answer.

NG/MJ passed with eight of eleven leverage despite both military refusals. I retain my judgment that it can work, but their objection to unequal institutional concessions remains unresolved. Guild repair under delegated authority and both Security delegates' actual agreements justified surrendering my command. The Guild supplied Lantern and upheld upkeep; the army offered both assets, guarded communities and accepted conditioning decline. Civilians paid the Raid's costs; I spent Grey Petrel and two foresight tokens.

Round one: Guild Trade drafts blocked my proposed Campaign, making the Security cover's Raid question immediately relevant. I bought R1-S and changed Military/Campaign to reserve Relief/council Raid, retaining Warrant. Its target condition enabled a concrete compromise. Losing one leverage point was justified by that operational use.

Round two: both Guild drafts paired Repair with Trade, exactly within R2-N's scope. I bought it to understand civilian supplies while Guard and Restraint were discussed. My Repair/Guard/no-Warrant draft did not change. The distribution information improved confidence and our accounting, rather than changing my orders. In retrospect its leverage cost bought less practical value; declining would have been defensible, although I did not know the answer beforehand.

I chose no NONE option. One token remained because only two purchases were allowed, not because I deliberately saved one. Next test: add one operational round under the ratified constitution to observe whether military dissent affects offers and whether joint Security can sustain cooperation without my intervention.
